{{Ring theory sidebar}}
In [[Abstract algebra|algebra]], the '''free product''' ('''[[coproduct]]''') of a family of [[associative algebra]]s <math>A_i, i \in I</math> over a [[commutative ring|commutative]] [[Ring (mathematics)|ring]] ''R'' is the associative algebra over ''R'' that is, roughly, defined by the generators and the relations of the <math>A_i</math>'s. The free product of two algebras ''A'', ''B'' is denoted by ''A''&thinsp;∗&thinsp;''B''. The notion is a [[Ring theory|ring-theoretic]] analog of a [[free product]] of [[Group (mathematics)|groups]].

In the [[Category of commutative algebras|category of commutative ''R''-algebras]], the free product of two algebras (in that [[Category (mathematics)|category]]) is their [[tensor product of algebras|tensor product]].

== Construction ==
We first define a free product of two algebras. Let ''A'' and ''B'' be algebras over a commutative ring ''R''. Consider their [[tensor algebra]], the direct sum of all possible finite tensor products of ''A'', ''B''; explicitly, <math>T = \bigoplus_{n=1}^{\infty} T_n</math> where
:<math>T_1 = A \oplus B, \,\, T_2 = (A \otimes A) \oplus (A \otimes B) \oplus (B \otimes A) \oplus (B \otimes B), \, \dots</math>

We then set
:<math>A * B = T/I</math>
where ''I'' is the two-sided [[Ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] generated by elements of the form
:<math>a \otimes a' - a a', \, b \otimes b' - bb', \, 1_A - 1_B.</math>

It is then straightforward to verify that the above construction possesses the [[Universal property|universal property]] of a coproduct.

A finite free product is defined similarly.<!-- no idea for infinite free product.
